newsitem.title: USA: Sonus rises on FDA ruling.
newsitem.headline: Sonus rises on FDA ruling.

text.p: Shares of Sonus Pharmaceuticals Inc rose sharply after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration determined that a new class of ultrasound contrast diagnostic agents be classified as drugs rather than medical devices. Sonus shares rose 2-3/8 to 33-1/8.
Analysts said the FDA determination puts Sonus back on track for a likely approval of its EchoGen contrast agent as early as the beginning of next year.
"I don't think there was much doubt it was going to get approved, but the timing was unclear," said Hambrecht and Quist analyst Alex Zisson.
"The FDA ruling starts the clock ticking again," Zisson added.

Sonus is one of a group of companies developing these ultrasound contrast agents for diagnostic purposes, but one competitor, Molecular Biosystems Inc, had filed for approval of its agent as a medical device. The medical device approval process is typically shorter than that for drugs.
"In retrospect the (FDA's) device division never should have accepted Molecular Biosystem's application," Zisson said. "It really stuck out like a sore thumb."

Zisson said the FDA ruling "moves the cloud off of Sonus and onto Molecular Biosystems," which is also moving through the FDA approval process but could face delays by having to reclassify its Optison agent as a drug.
Molecular Biosystems shares were down 1-7/16 to 8-7/16.
